task.title: Configuring a Guest Network
task.shortdesc: Configure a separate Wi-Fi network that gives visitors Internet access without giving them access to the primary home network or the router management interface.

prereq.p: Before you configure a guest network, make sure that:

ul.li: The is connected to the or Optical Network Terminal (ONT).
The primary Wi-Fi network is configured and operational.
A computer or mobile device is connected to the .
You have the credentials for the .
You have permission to change the network configuration.

prereq.note: Use a wired connection when possible. A wired connection remains active if the router restarts its wireless service.

context.p: A guest network provides Internet access to visitors through a separate wireless network. In this guide, the guest network uses the SSID .
A correctly isolated guest network prevents guest devices from accessing devices, shared resources, and management functions on the primary network.
context.note: Give visitors the guest network name and guest network password. Do not give visitors the password for .
Enable local network isolation and management interface restrictions. Enable client isolation if guest devices do not need to communicate with each other.

step.cmd: Open a supported web browser on the connected computer or mobile device.
Go to .
step.stepresult: The sign-in page for the opens.

step.cmd: Sign in to the .

substep.cmd: Enter in the user name field.
Enter the current administrator password.
Select Sign in.

step.cmd: Open the guest network settings.

info.p: The guest network settings can appear on the or the .
info.note: Menu and control names can differ by .

step.cmd: Enable the guest network.

info.p: The guest network controls become available after you enable the guest network.

step.cmd: Select the Wi-Fi band for the guest network.

info.p: Enable both supported bands when possible. This setting provides compatibility for different guest devices.
Enable the required bands from . A 2.4 GHz guest network can support older devices and provide more coverage. A 5 GHz guest network can provide increased throughput for compatible devices.

step.cmd: Set the guest network name to .

info.p: The guest network name appears in the list of available Wi-Fi networks on client devices.
info.note: Do not include a person's name, an address, a telephone number, a password, or other private information in the guest network name.

step.cmd: Set the guest network security mode to .

info.p: Use the strongest security mode supported by the and the required guest devices.
info.note: If a required guest device does not support WPA3, use WPA2/WPA3 transition mode when this option is available.
Do not configure the guest network as an open network. An open network permits devices to connect without a password.

step.cmd: Create a strong and unique

info.p: Use the password requirements shown in the .
Store the guest network password in a secure location.
info.note: Do not use the primary or the password for the as the guest network password.

step.cmd: Disable guest access to the primary network.

info.p: Disable controls such as Access Local Network, Access Intranet, or Allow Access to Local Devices.
info.note: Keep local network access disabled unless guest devices must use a specific local resource.

step.stepresult: Guest devices cannot access devices and shared resources on the primary network.

step.cmd: Disable access to router management functions from the guest network.

info.p: Guest devices must not have access to the , , or .

step.stepresult: Guest devices cannot use the guest network to change the router configuration.

step.cmd: Enable client isolation for the guest network.

info.p: Client isolation prevents a guest device from communicating directly with other devices on the same guest network.
The setting can appear as Client Isolation, AP Isolation, or Device Isolation.
info.note: Do not enable client isolation if guest devices must communicate with each other for an approved purpose.

step.cmd: Configure a bandwidth limit for the guest network if required.

info.p: Use the bandwidth controls to prevent guest traffic from using all available Internet capacity.
info.note: Select a limit that permits normal browsing and approved online services. A low limit can cause poor performance for guest devices.

step.cmd: Set the maximum number of guest devices if required.

info.p: Set a value that supports the expected number of visitors. Do not set a limit that is higher than the network can support.

step.cmd: Configure an operating schedule for the guest network if required.

info.p: Set the days and times when visitors require Internet access.
If a schedule is not required, disable the guest network when visitors no longer require access.

step.cmd: Review the guest network settings.

ul.li: The guest network uses a unique password.
Access to the primary network is disabled.
Access to router management functions is disabled.
Client isolation, bandwidth limits, device limits, and schedules have the required values.

step.cmd: Select Apply.

info.p: Wait while the applies the guest network settings.
info.note: The wireless service can stop temporarily while the router applies the settings.

step.cmd: Connect a test device to the guest network.

substep.cmd: Open the Wi-Fi settings on the test device.
Select .
Enter the guest network password.
Select the option to connect to the network.
Wait for the device to connect.

step.cmd: Verify Internet access from the test device.

substep.cmd: Open a supported web browser on the test device.
Open a trusted external website.
Confirm that the website opens without a connection error.

step.stepresult: The test device can access Internet services through the guest network.

step.cmd: Verify that the test device cannot access the primary network.

substep.cmd: Try to access a shared device or resource on the primary network.
Confirm that the test device cannot access the shared device or resource.

step.stepresult: The guest network prevents access to devices and resources on the primary network.

step.cmd: Verify that the test device cannot access the router management interface.

substep.cmd: Try to open from the test device.
Confirm that the does not open.

step.stepresult: The guest network prevents access to router management functions.

step.cmd: Verify client isolation if you enabled this setting.

substep.cmd: Connect a second test device to .
Try to communicate with the first test device from the second test device.
Confirm that the two guest devices cannot communicate directly.

step.stepresult: Client isolation prevents direct communication between guest devices.

step.cmd: Confirm that the test device appears on the .

substep.cmd: Connect an administrator device to the primary network.
Sign in to the .
Open the list of devices connected to the guest network.
Confirm that the test device appears in the list.

step.stepresult: The identifies the test device as a guest network device.

result.p: The guest network is operational. Guest devices can access Internet services but cannot access the primary network or router management functions.

postreq.p: After you configure the guest network:

ul.li: Store the guest network password in a secure location.
Share the password only with authorized visitors.
Review the guest device list on the regularly.
Block a device that you do not recognize.
Change the guest network password if an unauthorized user obtains it.
Disable the guest network when visitors do not require access.
